newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica under pressure to expel Mobutu's generals-paper.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica under pressure to expel Mobutu's generals-paper.

text.p: The government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is pressuring South Africa to expel generals loyal to former Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko who fled to the country with their loot, a Sunday newspaper reported.
The Sunday Independent said Laurent Kabila's new government claims the generals brought millions of dollars with them and were using South African soil to plot a coup against Kinshasa's rulers.

"We know that most of Mobutu's generals are here in South Africa and those who were criminals in Congo will continue to be criminals here. They dont't have any reason to be here," Congo Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha told the newspaper.

Karaha, who met his South African counterpart Alfred Nzo in Pretoria this week, added: "They are illegal in this country. They are carrying diplomatic passports which we revoked and I do not know what papers they are using. We have discussed this matter with the South African government, but I shall not tell you what we agreed to.
"If these people have been given refugee status, refugees are not politicians, so I don't see how they can conduct political activities," Karaha said.
Aziz Pahad, South African Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister, said: "We have to find out on what basis these people are here to ensure that no illegal activities are carried out from South African soil.
"If those people are illegal they must be returned to their countries or wherever they want to go," he said.
"Any Zaireans who conduct illegal activities or attempt to subvert another government will be dealt with as a matter of urgency."
Kabila, who toppled Mobutu in May, is scheduled to visit South Africa within the next few weeks.
